correctness.rationale: Algebraic identities show h=fg=gf is idempotent with unique fixed root per fiber, invariant under f and g. An element fixed only by one retraction maps under the other to its root; each remaining element chooses independently an f-image in the f-fixed set and a g-image in the g-fixed set. These choices and the labeled component decomposition are bijections, proving the formal EGF and recurrence for all n. The accompanying checker matches every (common rank, f rank, g rank) coefficient by independently testing all pairs for n<=5, and its recurrence yields A_0..A_10. Finite tests are corroboration, not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The object is a natural equational subclass in the two-function one-variable finite-model-count frontier, which otherwise contains fixed #P1-hard sentences. The composite-fiber normal form determines the full joint fixed-rank distribution rather than a single scalar enumeration; its explicit integer recurrence yields a polynomial-time exact count and supports conditioned model counting by three canonical invariants. It is not a renamed one-function enumeration or an arbitrary finite slice; old action-enumeration coverage remains a named scientific risk.
